title: Ordinary divided powers on an ideal
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset C$ an ideal. An ordinary divided-power structure on $I$ is a family of maps $\gamma_n:I\to I$ for $n\geq1$, with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, such that $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(cx)=c^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i=0}^n\gamma_i(x)\gamma_{n-i}(y)$, $\gamma_n(x)\gamma_m(x)=\binom{n+m}{n}\gamma_{n+m}(x)$ and $\gamma_n(\gamma_m(x))=\frac{(nm)!}{n!(m!)^n}\gamma_{nm}(x)$ for $c\in C$, $x,y\in I$ and positive $n,m$. The factorial quotient is an integer, acting by repeated addition. Equivalently use total maps $\operatorname{dpow}:\mathbb N\to C\to C$ by extending the maps by zero off $I$; on $I$ the zeroth map is 1 and every positive map takes values in $I$. This is the ordinary ideal structure on $A_{\mathrm{even},+}\subset A_{\mathrm{even}}$ appearing in [def-sfb-graded-divided-power-structure]; the graded notion additionally imposes homogeneity and vanishing on products of homogeneous odd elements.
